section.title: Cost analysis
section.label: Cost analysis
section.summary: A staged three-station planning budget combining sourced equipment prices with explicit internal allowances.

paragraphs.text: Capital expenditure (CAPEX) covers equipment and setup; operating expenditure (OPEX) covers services while active. Q190 core equipment is 13,933,146 VND per station, or 43,482,944 VND for three stations and one optional shared pH kit. These hardware subtotals exclude the remaining pilot costs. The budget uses a historical 25,940 VND/USD assumption, not a current transaction rate.

paragraphs.text: The 36-month project starts one station before two more at illustrative month six. The 100W/40Ah power configuration and unquoted items are planning assumptions. Listed prices, market benchmarks and internal allowances are distinguished in Appendix E; simulated results do not establish field performance.

Table 4 estimates 339,314,885 VND including 20% contingency. Its low–high scenarios reflect different allowances, not guaranteed prices. Labour uses 600,000 VND per person-day, informed by published electrical-work benchmarks. Future prices are held constant for comparison.

paragraphs.text: Thirty-six monthly field rounds include pH calibration, DO cleaning and the six testing rounds; 16 station checks are not extra journeys. Early DO/turbidity calibration every two months stays within 90 days. Shared hosting is counted once. Renewal, incidents, delivery, supply-tax uncertainty and disposal have separate allowances; full-probe DO reserves cover unavailable cap pricing.

paragraphs.text: A proposed municipal or institutional pilot fund would cover setup. Operations and renewal average about 5.31 million VND per project-month before contingency. This proposal charges households no monitoring fee and assumes no grant, income or unpaid labour. These are proposed funding roles, not commitments; income evidence does not establish affordability. If recurring funding is insufficient, retain one pilot and defer expansion.

Ordering the next two stations requires acceptance and an updated budget. Field power, coverage and repair capacity remain untested; the 48-hour response target is not a contracted service. Contingency does not guarantee performance or unlimited incident coverage.

Six testing rounds and 16 station checks are included in those visits. Hardware renewal figures are funding reserves, not failure predictions.
